1) Primary deletion: once we request tenant data deletion for hosted API, what is the SLA for removing conversational content and embeddings from primary stores?

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below so your team can paste into the questionnaire; I looped in our security and legal leads for technical and contractual specifics. I attached a short summary PDF for reviewers.

1) Primary deletion: We remove tenant conversational content and embeddings from primary serving stores within 30 calendar days after a deletion request. In most cases (standard API customers) deletions complete within 7–14 days depending on in-flight requests and cache flushing.

2) Backups & snapshots: We maintain encrypted backups for disaster recovery. Customer-identifying data is removed from backups on a 90-day scrub schedule; deletion requests trigger a flag to accelerate removal in the next backup cycle and start an expedited scrub for the affected tenant.

3) Regional handback: For EU-bound exports we provide NDJSON or Parquet bundles, plus a CSV index. Typical turnaround is 5 business days for a full tenant export; expedited exports (48–72 hours) available under Dedicated/Enterprise contracts.

4) Certification / evidence: We can provide a deletion confirmation letter and export checksum. All deletion/export operations produce audit-log entries (request id, actor, timestamps). We can provide a filtered audit-log extract under NDA.

5) Key management: BYOK is available for Enterprise customers (KMS/HSM integration). For Hosted tier we manage encryption keys but offer strict separation and rotation policies; we can discuss a KMS onboarding timeline if you prefer BYOK.

I've attached: Redwood_Data_Disposition_Summary.pdf (one-page summary). Irene will follow up with more technical detail and Karthik will propose contractual language for deletion timelines and attestations.

Next step: if that looks good, can we schedule a 30-minute call this week to finalize the wording in your RFP?

Thanks,

Hi Elena — quick technical addendum to Marissa's notes: please feel free to paste these into the technical appendix.

Primary stores and caches
- Conversations and embeddings are stored in sharded primary stores with ephemeral cache layers. When a deletion request is received we take three parallel actions: (1) mark tenant ID as deleted in the routing layer, (2) purge KV/prefix caches immediately, (3) enqueue primary-store deletion tasks.
- Active requests in-flight are allowed to finish; we block new requests for that tenant shortly after request receipt to avoid re-ingestion.

Backups & snapshots
- Backups are encrypted at rest with AES-256. Backups are incremental; objects referencing tenant IDs are tracked by metadata to allow selective scrub. Our standard retention is 90 days, but we maintain a backup retention matrix depending on customer tier and region.
- On deletion request we flag all backup metadata for the tenant; sanitization starts at the next backup rewrite cycle. For critical escalations we can initiate an out-of-cycle rewrite (subject to contractual SLA).

Auditability & evidence
- All deletion/export operations emit an immutable audit record (request id, initiating account, S3 artifact id, job status). We can provide signed export checksums and a scoped audit-log extract.

Regional considerations
- For EU-region tenants we support region-pin options; export packages are generated in-region and transferred via secure presigned URLs.

Key management
- BYOK: we support customer KMS keys (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). When BYOK is enabled, the key unwrap/rotation policy is jointly governed and deletion of key material is a separate contractual commitment.

I attached our operational diagram for the hosted API flow which highlights where deletion hooks run.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena / Marissa — adding the legal framing you can use in the SOW / contract appendix. Draft phrasing below and attached a redlineable Word draft.

- Deletion SLA: Redwood will permanently remove customer-identifiable content from primary serving stores within 30 calendar days of a validated deletion request. Parties may agree to accelerated timelines for Dedicated contracts.
- Backup scrub: Redwood shall remove or render unrecoverable customer-identifiable data from backups within 90 calendar days of deletion request, except where longer retention is required by law.
- Export & handback: Redwood will provide tenant data exports in NDJSON or Parquet, with optional CSV index. Standard delivery: within 5 business days; expedited delivery (48–72 hours) available for Enterprise customers.
- Attestation & evidence: Upon request Redwood will provide (a) a signed deletion attestation letter, (b) export package checksum(s), and (c) a filtered audit-log extract covering the deletion/export job. Attestation requests will be fulfilled within 7 business days of request.
- Key management: When BYOK is elected, customer controls encryption keys; Redwood will provide technical assistance for key rotation and will not retain plaintext key material.

If ArgusAI requires more stringent guarantees (e.g., escrow, certified destruction by a third party), we can include an addendum; I attached Data_Deletion_Addendum_draft.docx for negotiation. Also adding a placeholder DocuSign link for the addendum if you'd like to proceed.

Regards,
